newsitem.title: USA: Federated, EchoStar focus of US corporate bonds.
newsitem.headline: Federated, EchoStar focus of US corporate bonds.

text.p: Federated Department Stores and Viacom Inc bonds surged while EchoStar Communications Corp DISH.O junk bonds fizzled on Friday, in an otherwise quiet day of trading in the U.S. corporate bond markets, traders said.
New corporate bond issuance also tapered off, as is typical toward the end of the week, market sources said.

In the high-yield market, Cityscape Financial, a sub-prime mortgage lender, sold $300 million in senior notes, rated B1/B, to yield 12.75 percent in a 144a private placement via CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp.
In a written statement, Fitch stated, "The rating is based on the improved operating results due to the successful integration of R.H. Macy and The Braodway into Federated."
Traders said spreads on the company's bonds tightened 12-15 basis points on the news.

In other news, direct broadcast satellite company (DBS) company, EchoStar Communications, announced on Friday that it would ask a court to determine whether News Corp was obliged to loan the company $200 million under the terms of a proposed merger agreement.
The news fueled the perception that the two companies will be unable to resolve their differences to complete the proposed merger.
EchoStar 12 7/8 percent zero coupon bonds dropped to 80-81 from and 83 bid while its 13 1/8 percent zero coupon bonds dropped to 68-69 from 72-72.5, a high-yield source said.
G. Robert Berzins, high-yield media analyst at Lehman Brothers Inc, said the probability of a deal now seems low.
However, he said the fundamental value of the bonds is attractive at current price levels.
"The value of EchoStar's assets provides very good protection for bondholders," he said. "The company has assets worth close to $2 billion and only about $800 million in debt."

Elsewhere, spreads on Viacom long-term debt tightened by roughly eight basis points on a Wall Street Journal report that Seagram Co Ltd's Universal Studios is prepared to buy the company's half of USA Networks, according to people familiar with the deal.
In the overall market, spreads on investment-grade corporates remained unchanged on moderate trading.
High-yield bond prices also finished the day flat on typically sluggish Friday trading.
In other markets, the Dow Jones industrial average rose 30.92 points to finish at 7169.54

The price of the benchmark 10-year Treasury rose 16/32 to 99-22/32, pushing the yield down to 6.67 percent. The price of the benchmark 30-year long-bond ended the day 17/32 higher at 96-20/32. Its yield fell to 6.89 percent.
